name: Muhamed Isabegovic
title: Staff Engineer
summary: I have spent ten years making software and leading the teams that make it, from deciding what to build to running it in production. I have worked across the stack: trading systems in C++, SaaS products in Ruby on Rails, AI features in hiring software, and data pipelines with AI agents. The largest team I led was around 30 engineers, fully remote across seven time zones. These days I work with agents writing the code, and I build open-source tools that keep that code reliable.

experience.title: Staff Engineer and Founder
experience.summary: My own company. Since 2025 I work through it on B2B contracts as a staff engineer and technical lead; the roles below were delivered through it. It also runs RubyConf Austria and my product Usput.ba, and in 2024 it ran EuRuKo 2024 alongside my role at Meisterlabs.

experience.title: Staff Engineer
experience.summary: AI-native engineering company building software and AI for enterprises, high-growth startups and private equity portfolio companies.
bullets: Took over a proof of concept with my team, working inside the client's team, and brought it to stable production with observability for its pipelines and agents. Helped set the technical direction.
Built the data pipelines on Azure and Microsoft Fabric in a medallion architecture: PySpark notebooks bring multiple sources together, and knowledge graphs in FalkorDB sit on top.

Built AI agents that enrich and classify the data, on OpenAI models in Microsoft Foundry. They use OpenAI's Decisions API for fast, typed decisions, and MCP servers give them the graph and the data as tools.
Introduced AI-native delivery in my team: agents write the code, people shape and review it. Helped the client's engineers bring AI into their own development lifecycle.

experience.title: AI Product Developer
experience.summary: ATS serving 8,500+ companies, on Rails and Ember.js, with retrieval (RAG) on pgvector in the AI features. I owned AI features from pitch and spec to rollout and measurement, working in Shape Up.
bullets: Shipped "Request Missing Information" to all customers: it spots what an application lacks, has an LLM draft a short questionnaire for the candidate, writes the answers back and re-runs screening.
Rebuilt AI screening on the trigger system, so recruiters can screen at any stage and save criteria on job templates. Backfilled every company and rolled it out to all customers.
Moved the AI features' prompts into Langfuse, with datasets, LLM judges and live scoring on production traffic. Ran A/B experiments of prompt and model versions there and promoted the winners.
Shipped automatic candidate moves based on the screening outcome, a customer request. Made screening wait until the CV is parsed, so nobody is screened before their CV is read.

experience.title: Consultant
experience.summary: Speech-to-text app for doctors: AI work, architecture review, and product vision with the founder.

experience.title: Technical Lead
experience.summary: Seed-stage AI platform for recruiters; Carv acquired it two months after I joined.
bullets: Led two teams, one on the Rails product that came from Recrubo and one on Carv's Node.js/TypeScript product, owning delivery together with a product manager.
Led the integration of both products after the acquisition: one Vue.js frontend, a shared database for clients and login sessions, and common ATS integrations.
Co-built and maintained the event-driven system on Redis Pub/Sub that connects the two stacks and carries new functionality, with Google Cloud Tasks as a fallback and for workload management.

Built the data pipelines that bring jobs, candidates and applications in from 20+ applicant tracking systems, normalise them into one model and pass them on to the AI features, which use retrieval (RAG) on pgvector. AI features worked the same for every client, and adding a new ATS didn't mean new code elsewhere.
Introduced spec-driven development in both teams: features are written up as specs and agreed first, then implemented with coding agents and reviewed by engineers.

Owned DevOps and CI/CD on Google Cloud, with monitoring and observability for the parts my teams ran, and ran integration and background work on Google Cloud Functions, triggered by events and queues or on a schedule.

experience.title: AI Engineer
experience.summary: A travel guide to Bosnia and Herzegovina with thousands of visits a month, which I build and run alone on Rails and Hotwire, deployed with Kamal. It is where I try AI features on real users first.
bullets: Built generation grounded in real data (RAG, on pgvector). Place descriptions, audio-tour scripts and itineraries are written from places retrieved from a places API and the site's own database, not from the model's memory.
Built the LLM layer on RubyLLM with schema-enforced structured output, layered retries, JSON repair and versioned prompts, configured for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini models.
Wrote a tested MCP server in plain Ruby, with a rule-based validator that catches made-up details in records the model creates.

experience.title: Conference organiser
experience.at: EuRuKo 2024; founder of RubyConf Austria and GoatConf
bullets: EuRuKo 2024, Sarajevo: 3 days, 3 tracks, 50 speakers from 25+ countries, 700 attendees.

RubyConf Austria 2026, Vienna: about 200 attendees and 13 speakers, with workshops and a community day built around a treasure hunt app I wrote (hunt.rubyconf.at). GoatConf follows in June 2027 in Tuzla.
Led both end to end, budget and sponsorships included, with a small volunteer team.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
experience.summary: Maker of MindMeister and MeisterTask. I worked on MindMeister and the accounts system, in Rails and React, with MySQL and Sidekiq.
bullets: Proposed, designed and built a plans and permissions system shared by Accounts, MindMeister and MeisterTask. It replaced feature checks hardcoded across the apps, so the product team could set up plans and run billing experiments without developer time.

Built MindMeister product features for three years and ran A/B experiments across markets: on pricing and plans, paywalls and upgrade prompts, onboarding and sign-up, and new features before their full release.

Maintained, monitored and expanded the Kubernetes setup for MindMeister: its dashboards, metrics and alerts, the Helm charts and deployment configuration, and new services and environments. Split backend and frontend deployments into separate pipelines, so the frontend went from weekly releases tied to the backend to daily ones.

experience.title: Engineering Manager
experience.summary: An ATS for tech and data-science hiring: three Ember.js apps on a Ruby on Rails monolith, with PostgreSQL on Kubernetes. I returned as lead after joining as a junior engineer in 2016.
bullets: Led the engineering team as it grew from about 12 to about 30 engineers across backend, frontend and DevOps, fully remote over 7 time zones. Everyone reported to me, and I reported to the founders.

Was the bridge between the founders and the engineers: agreed priorities, timelines and trade-offs with the founders, product and design, and sales, and turned them into a technical direction the team delivered.
Formed an architecture committee. Its members became the tech leads I trusted to shape work and lead delivery.
Hired for part of that growth: designed the hiring process, ran technical interviews, made the hiring decisions and onboarded the new engineers.

Introduced and ran the team's processes: sprint planning and estimation, retrospectives, roadmap and release planning, and the rules for code review and releases. They kept delivery on schedule while the team more than doubled.
Took part in the architecture work throughout: the API between the Ember.js apps and the Rails monolith, framework upgrades, and database and performance work.
Stayed hands-on: built core backend features and the recruiter and candidate dashboards, reviewed most of the code, and worked on infrastructure and CI/CD with our DevOps engineer.

experience.title: C++ Software Engineer
bullets: Built trading algorithms and worked on the analytics platform traders used, in C++ on a real-time system built on the actor model (C++ Actor Framework).
Built a Python test environment that emulated markets and simulated trading systems, so algorithms could be tested without live markets.

experience.title: Junior Software Engineer
experience.summary: Joined as a junior engineer; returned in 2019 as lead.

open_source.name: empty-shell
open_source.text: A starting repository for projects run with a coding agent: rules, checks and an empty wiki, with enola, tabula and taha inside.

open_source.name: enola
open_source.text: Checks a codebase's architecture rules in CI. I built its rule system and maintain four Ruby gems that bring it to Rails teams.

open_source.name: tabula
open_source.text: A Rust tool that keeps a project's memory and decisions as plain files in git, and judges finished work against what was decided.

open_source.name: taha
open_source.text: Runs a coding agent unattended inside a mandate you set, and comes back with finished, checked work.

open_source.name: enola-guides
open_source.text: Guides to enola for Rails, Ember, Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust, with a catalogue of 26 architecture laws. Ten releases since August 2026, on RubyGems, npm, PyPI and crates.io.

open_source.name: tended and pi-brain
open_source.text: Knowledge bases a coding agent maintains, so people and agents work from the same written specs and decisions. tended is on PyPI; pi-brain is on npm, with ten releases.

open_source.name: treasure_hunt
open_source.text: A location-based treasure hunt for conferences, built on Rails 8.1 for RubyConf Austria 2026 and open-sourced under MIT.

recommendations.text: The word that best describes Muhamed is 'visionary'. I had the pleasure of co-organising RubyConf Austria with him. For more than a year, I watched Muhamed take ideas that sounded wildly unreasonable and somehow make them a reality. His standard response was: 'Don't worry about it. It's going to be fine. We'll deal with it.' When things went wrong, Muhamed stayed calm, made a decision and got moving. He expected a great deal from himself while remaining patient and generous with everyone around him. His enthusiasm pushed the whole team to aim higher, and he was genuinely fun to work with. Muhamed is a kind and capable leader. I would gladly work with him again. I have merely learned to be careful when he begins a sentence with, 'I have an idea.'

I worked with Muhamed on the same team for a year, and he quickly became one of the people I relied on most. Muhamed leads by doing. When we hit a hard problem, he didn't start with a long discussion. He wrote the code, showed it working, and then we talked. That habit moved the team forward more than once. He is a strong Ruby on Rails engineer and a natural architect. He took on leading the technical direction and shaping the code, and his decisions held up as the project grew. No challenge was too big or too unfamiliar for him. He is resourceful and knowledgeable, and when the answer wasn't obvious, he knew where to look. He is precise and professional, and he holds a high bar. He is also direct. When something wasn't good enough, he said so plainly, even when that was hard to hear. It was always about the work and never about the person, and it made both our code and our team better. I would gladly work with Muhamed again, and I recommend him to any team that needs a Rails engineer who can lead.

Muhamed is one of the most amazing professionals I have ever worked with. He is extremely talented, dependable, and disciplined. Moreover, he is always willing to push himself beyond limits to make a product successful. With Muhamed's excellent communication and engineering management skills everything is possible. At Experfy, Muhamed single-handedly managed the team collaboration consisting of 7+ timezones. He has a vast reservoir of talent - enabling him to lead Backend, Frontend, and DevOps teams with flying colors. In design thinking sessions, Muhamed played a vital role with his powerful insight about the product roadmap and technical knowledge. As an engineering manager, he always backed his team with full support. In addition to these Muhamed conducted extremely high-yielding Sprint retrospectives. He was always willing to go the extra mile to increase productivity and eliminate blockers. I would strongly recommend Muhamed and would love to work with him again.
